name: Vonoprazan
summary: A potassium-competitive acid blocker: acid-stable, reversible, and effective from the first dose without needing an acidic environment to activate.
good: Refractory GERD, nocturnal acid breakthrough on a PPI, or H. pylori regimens where faster, deeper acid suppression improves antibiotic efficacy.
bad: Newer agent — less long-term outcome data than decades-old PPIs; availability and cost vary by region.
clinicalPearls: Because a PCAB doesn’t need an acidic canaliculus to switch on, it sidesteps the exact mechanism that makes PPIs slow to reach full effect and blind to nocturnal pumps.
mechanism: Reversible, competitive inhibition of the H⁺/K⁺-ATPase at the potassium-binding site — no acid-catalyzed activation required, unlike PPIs.
pharmacodynamics: More potent and more consistent acid suppression than PPIs, including better nocturnal control, from the first dose.

pharmacokinetics.onset: Rapid — near-maximal effect on day one, since activation doesn’t depend on cumulative pump turnover across several doses.
pharmacokinetics.duration: Long duration of action from a single dose; suppression doesn’t taper as the drug is cleared the way PPI benefit is capped by pump half-life.
pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Primarily CYP3A4, with additional non-CYP pathways; far less affected by CYP2C19 genotype than PPIs.

indications: GERD and erosive esophagitis; increasingly used in H. pylori eradication regimens, including against strains showing reduced PPI-based regimen efficacy.
interactionNotes: Fewer CYP2C19-driven concerns than PPIs, but CYP3A4 interactions (e.g., strong inducers/inhibitors) are relevant.
